'''Haiza''', officially the '''United Republic of Haiza''', is a country in [[North Massir]] along the [[Zhalrn mountains]] region. It is bordered by the [[Ucrua]] to the northwest, [[Diairesi Sea]] to the northeast, the [[Kera Sea]] to the east, [[Migoku]] to the south, and [[Shinam]] to the west. According to a 1765 estimate, Haiza has a [[List of countries and dependencies by population|population of around 20.6 million]].

Many important [[hominid fossils]] have been found in Haiza. In the Stone and Bronze Age, [[prehistoric migrations]] into Haiza included the [[Kowniss]] peoples, who moved south from present-day Jshain; Eastern [[Nahlsc]] people who moved into Haiza from the [[Siishchi peoples|Siishchi]] about 1,000 and 2,000 years ago; and the [[Southern Niles peoples|Southern Niles]], including the [[Daoaiq peoples|Daoaiq]], who originated from the present-day [[Ihner–Migoku border]] region between 2,900 and 2,400 years ago.  These movements took place at about the same time as the settlement of the [[Xhehuewd]] from south [[Massir]]. Between 400 BFA and 1000AFA, periodic coastal settlements by [[Taval|Tavalan]] merchants had dominated the coastline. It was properly conquered in the 11th century under the [[Askye Kingdom]], and later [[Askye Empire]]. In the late 19th century, the mainland came under Lycroa rule as [[Lycroan Eeuerlos Colony]]. This was followed by [[Emara|Emaran rule]] after the [[Great Imperial War]], when it was governed as Hazia, with [[Jshain]] remaining a part of the colonial jurisdiction. Following independence in 1712, [[Jshain]] fought a guerrilla war against the new Haizan government, gaining their respective independence in 1714.

Today, the country is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_republic presidential constitutional republic] with the [[federal capital]] located in Government City ([[Chavira]]); the former capital, [[Tijhara]], retains most government offices and is the country's largest city, principal port, and leading commercial centre. For decades, Haiza has been ruled by the [[Suin Tir Hoyabi]] (STH) as a de facto one-party state.

Haiza's population comprises about [[120 ethnic, linguistic, and religious groups]]. ____ is the largest religion in Haiza, with substantial ____ and ____ minorities. Over [[100 languages]] are spoken in Haiza, making it the most linguistically diverse country in [[North Massir]]. The country does not have a de jure official language, although the national language is [[Haizan language|Haizan]]. [[Alqiran language|Alqiran]] is used in foreign trade, in diplomacy, in higher courts, and as a medium of instruction in secondary and higher education. [[Iroan language|Iroan]] is widely spoken in the north, reflecting its history as a trading centre dominated by [[Taval|Tavalans]].

Haiza's economy is the largest in [[North Massir]], with [[Tijhara]] serving as a major regional commercial hub. With a [[List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita|per-capita GDP]] of {{Lahn}}4,722, the country is a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country lower-middle-income economy]. Agriculture is the country's largest economic sector; fish and fruit are the sector's traditional cash crops, while fresh flowers are a [[fast-growing export]]. The service industry, particularly tourism, is also one of the country's major economic drivers. [[Haiza]] is a member of the [[North Massiran Community]] trade bloc. [[Ayuma]] is Haiza's largest export market, followed by [[Dahe]].
